rules.status: Useful if a dietary gap exists
rules.reason: Protein powder can help fill a known dietary protein gap. If food already meets your needs, adding powder is optional.

rules.status: Optional performance add-on
rules.reason: Creatine monohydrate has evidence for repeated high-intensity exercise and resistance-training adaptations. It is not required to begin training.

rules.status: Consider dietary context first
rules.reason: Low fish intake is a reason to review dietary omega-3 sources, not proof that a fish-oil supplement will prevent disease. Compare verified EPA+DHA.

rules.status: Discuss before adding
rules.reason: Some short trials suggest benefits for stress or sleep with specific extracts. Long-term safety and equivalence across products remain uncertain.

rules.status: Use for an established need
rules.reason: A bone-health goal alone does not establish vitamin D deficiency or justify a high-strength product. Confirm the need and suitable formulation with a clinician.

rules.status: Not an automatic sleep or recovery add-on
rules.reason: Review dietary intake and an established reason for supplementation. A salt name or elemental amount does not establish a sleep benefit.

rules.status: Combination requires individual review
rules.reason: Assess calcium, magnesium and zinc separately. A combined tablet is not automatically better than addressing an individual dietary gap.

rules.status: Limited evidence: review the claim first
rules.reason: Small oral trials report mixed biomarker and cosmetic findings. They do not establish a general detox, disease-prevention or lasting skin-lightening benefit. Discuss a specific concern with a dermatologist; no product is added automatically.

rules.status: Review the sleep problem and timing first
rules.reason: Melatonin is relevant to some circadian problems, not every poor night or chronic insomnia. Timing, release form, medicines and the cause of sleep difficulty need review. It is not automatically combined with other sleep supplements.

rules.status: Check the need and laboratory-test implications
rules.reason: Evidence for routine hair or nail benefits without biotin deficiency is limited. Biotin can distort some laboratory tests. Review the cause of symptoms and disclose all biotin products to the testing team; no pack is added automatically.

rules.status: Review dietary supply before adding strength
rules.reason: Vitamin C can address inadequate intake, but routine high-strength use is not a general cold-prevention plan. Review food sources, clinical context and overlapping ingredients before choosing a product.

rules.status: Identify the individual vitamin requirement
rules.reason: B vitamins are distinct nutrients; a B-complex is not a diagnosis or an automatic energy treatment. People avoiding animal foods need a reliable B12 source. Review individual needs, possible absorption issues and total B6 or niacin before adding products.

rules.status: Review folate form and the reason for use
rules.reason: Folic acid has a specific prevention role for women who could become pregnant; it is not interchangeable with every folate form or DFE label. Discuss an appropriate plan and B12 context with a clinician. The tool does not prescribe a pregnancy product or strength.

rules.status: Review the nitric-oxide claim
rules.reason: A nitric-oxide pathway does not guarantee better exercise performance. Evidence is uncertain and a positive synthesis has methodological concerns. Check overlap with a pre-workout and its individually declared arginine before considering an extra product.

rules.status: Fat transport is not a fat-loss guarantee
rules.reason: Weight trials show a small average effect with variable results, not rapid or guaranteed fat burning. Healthy people generally make sufficient carnitine. Review the exact compound and the broader nutrition plan before considering a product.

rules.status: Review complete protein before isolated BCAA
rules.reason: BCAA provide only three of the nine essential amino acids. Acute signals do not establish extra long-term gains on top of adequate complete protein. Protein, EAA and BCAA overlap; these review items are not a three-product stack.

rules.status: Assess the full amino-acid and dietary need
rules.reason: All nine EAA support protein synthesis, but a separate EAA product is not automatically useful when food and complete protein already cover requirements. BCAA are included within EAA; assess protein, EAA and BCAA as overlapping sources.

rules.status: Inspect the formula and total stimulant exposure
rules.reason: Formulas vary and ingredient evidence does not validate every blend. Review caffeine from coffee, energy drinks and supplements, plus duplicate creatine or arginine and any second pre-workout. Unknown ingredient amounts prevent a reliable total; no stimulant product or dose is added automatically.

rules.status: Review form and uncertain performance benefit
rules.reason: Citrulline-malate findings suggest at most a small, uncertain average benefit. Full malate compound mass is not verified free L-citrulline. Review overlap with arginine and pre-workout; these are options to assess, not automatic additions.

rules.status: Match the exercise task and repeated-use evidence
rules.reason: Beta-alanine can raise muscle carnosine with repeated use and may help selected high-intensity tasks. Immediate tingling does not prove benefit. Account for beta-alanine already in pre-workout and review whether the goal fits the evidence.

rules.status: Assess isolated taurine separately from stimulants
rules.reason: Isolated taurine has limited, inconsistent exercise evidence and is distinct from caffeine. A result from an energy drink cannot be assigned to taurine alone. Review taurine and caffeine already present in pre-workout or other drinks before considering another product.

rules.status: Separate TMG exercise claims from betaine HCl
rules.reason: Some anhydrous betaine/TMG trials report specific strength benefits, but broad performance evidence remains uncertain. Betaine HCl digestive claims are a separate issue. Review exact form and overlap with pre-workout; no product or digestive treatment is added automatically.

rules.status: Review population, nutrition and exact HMB form
rules.reason: HMB evidence differs by setting and interpretation. Recent training meta-analyses do not show a routine added benefit, while some position statements are more favorable. Distinguish free-acid from calcium-HMB amounts and do not treat HMB, leucine, BCAA and EAA as equivalent exposures.

rules.status: Review the evidence and exact preparation
rules.reason: Collagen peptides, gelatin and native undenatured type II are different preparations. Evidence for skin or joint outcomes is formulation-specific and uncertain; symptom or laboratory changes do not prove cartilage regrowth or injury healing. Collagen is not an equivalent replacement for a complete dietary protein. Dated collagen pack data is available for manual comparison after the evidence guide. No automatic collagen product addition or quantity is assigned.

productPolicy.summary: These are the same checks used by the stack builder after its goal, health-context, existing-product and dietary-gap checks.
productPolicy.limitations: A matching label and price do not establish independent batch testing, authenticity, efficacy or suitability for an individual. Review uncertainty and the original sources before buying.
productPolicy.orderNote: Eligible packs are ordered by upfront pack price. Compare cost per labelled active amount and the full intended purchase before deciding; price order is not an efficacy or quality score.

common.label: A matching, dated price
common.detail: The recorded price must have evidence for the exact product and pack. Check its observation date; a catalog observation is not a live checkout quote.

common.label: Recorded as in stock
common.detail: Only offers recorded as in stock enter a purchase shortlist. Confirm availability and final price before buying.

common.label: No unresolved catalog field errors
common.detail: The dataset must pass its field validation. This checks recorded values; it does not establish independent purity testing, authenticity or clinical suitability.

common.label: Fits the pack budget you enter
common.detail: When an upfront budget is entered, each candidate pack must fit it. The review also totals selected packs, so several individually affordable packs can still exceed the combined budget.

protein.label: Known cost of actual labelled protein
protein.detail: Protein content must be established so cost per gram of protein can be calculated. Powder weight and scoop size alone do not establish protein content.

protein.label: Milk allergy or uncertain traces need review
protein.detail: The builder pauses protein-pack suggestions when milk allergy or uncertain traces are flagged; a plant ingredient class alone is not allergen certification.

protein.label: Plant protein when plant ingredients are requested
protein.detail: For a vegan ingredient preference, the listed protein type must be plant-based. This is an ingredient filter, not independent vegan certification.

creatine.label: Creatine monohydrate
creatine.detail: The automatic shortlist uses monohydrate. Evidence and equal-gram prices must not be transferred automatically to HCl, nitrate or other compounds.

creatine.label: {value}% labelled monohydrate
creatine.detail: The shortlist uses the recorded {value}% concentration. This is a label claim, not a laboratory purity certificate.

creatine.label: Unflavoured formula
creatine.detail: The shortlist uses unflavoured offers so flavoured blend weight does not complicate this comparison.

fish-oil.label: Compatible with the stated diet
fish-oil.detail: Fish-oil purchase suggestions are shown only for the no-ingredient-preference option. Vegetarian or vegan preferences stay in educational review.

fish-oil.label: Fish allergy or uncertainty needs review
fish-oil.detail: Fish-oil purchase suggestions pause when a fish allergy or uncertainty is reported.

fish-oil.label: EPA+DHA content is known
fish-oil.detail: Compare the declared EPA plus DHA, not the total fish-oil milligrams or ALA content.

fish-oil.label: Units per label serving are known
fish-oil.detail: A capsule count is not a serving count. Verified units per serving are needed to calculate pack servings and cost per EPA+DHA amount.
